findings.problem: ShardWorkflow uses raw String for status and separate bools for is_validated/is_sent instead of typed enums/typestates. This allows illegal states like status="sent" with is_validated=false, status="pending" with is_sent=true, or any arbitrary string value.
findings.failure_mode: Data integrity violation: downstream consumers cannot trust the status field or the boolean flags. A shard can appear sent without being validated, or carry a status string that does not correspond to any real workflow state.
findings.fix: Replace status: String with an enum (e.g. enum ShardStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent }) and replace is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool with a single status enum or a typestate struct (ShardWorkflowValidated / ShardWorkflowSent). Make all fields private and construct via fallible constructors.

findings.problem: All fields of ShardWorkflow are pub, exposing the internal representation and allowing external code to mutate fields directly without any invariant checking.
findings.failure_mode: External code can set item.is_sent = true without going through mark_sent(), or set status to an invalid string, bypassing all validation and creating illegal states at any call site.
findings.fix: Make all fields private (pub(crate) at most) and provide constructors, accessors, and state-transition methods only.

findings.problem: mark_sent has no precondition checks. It unconditionally overwrites status and is_sent without verifying the shard was validated or that it was not already sent. The function accepts a by-value ShardWorkflow but returns the same type, losing any typestate guarantee.
findings.failure_mode: A shard that was never validated can be marked sent. A shard already sent can be 're-sent'. No idempotency guard, no error return, no typed enforcement of the valid state transition (pending->validated->sent).
findings.fix: Use a typestate pattern: have separate types (ShardWorkflowValidated) with a mark_sent method that returns a new ShardWorkflowSent type. Or at minimum, return Result<ShardWorkflow, ShardError> and check current status before transitioning.

findings.problem: status (String), is_validated (bool), and is_sent (bool) encode overlapping state. Three fields for one concept create inevitable inconsistency and make it impossible to enforce a clean state machine.
findings.failure_mode: State desynchronization: is_sent=true and status="pending" can coexist, or is_validated=true with status="pending". Any code checking only one field may make incorrect decisions.
findings.fix: Collapse into a single enum ShardStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent } that encodes all three dimensions. Remove is_validated and is_sent entirely.

findings.problem: mark_sent returns ShardWorkflow directly with no error type. Even if preconditions existed, there is no way to communicate failure (e.g., already sent, not validated).
findings.failure_mode: Silent misbehavior: callers cannot distinguish success from attempted invalid transition. The function may silently do nothing useful or produce an inconsistent state.
findings.fix: Define a ShardError enum (AlreadySent, NotValidated) and change the signature to fn mark_sent(item: ShardWorkflowValidated) -> Result<ShardWorkflow, ShardError>.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms field exists but is never written to or read in mark_sent(). The timestamp for when a shard was sent is recorded nowhere, making auditability impossible.
findings.failure_mode: Lost audit trail: no record of when a shard was sent, preventing debugging, compliance checks, or replay analysis.
findings.fix: Set sent_at_epoch_ms = current_time_ms() in mark_sent() and make mark_sent return the updated ShardWorkflow. Add a current_time source abstraction (e.g., FnMut() -> u64) for testability.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent performance
no profiler or allocation evidence for ShardWorkflow size or mark_sent allocation pattern
no second-ring test or behavior test validating state transition invariants
no command evidence (no cargo test, cargo clippy, or cargo bench runs available)
residual_risk: Static review only with no commands run. The entire domain model is structurally non-compliant with Holzman Rust: no typestate enforcement, no error types, redundant state fields, and pub fields enabling illegal states at any call site. A complete typestate redesign is required before this module is acceptable for delivery.
